cohort: The study cohort consisted of 154 patients who underwent robotic-assisted laparoscopic hysterectomy (RALH) and 57 patients who underwent transvaginal robotic-assisted laparoscopic hysterectomy (tVRALH) for benign gynecologic diseases.
finding: Patients undergoing tVRALH tended to have a lower BMI, a higher proportion of history of vaginal delivery, a lower proportion of history of cesarean delivery, lighter uterine weight, less blood loss, and shorter operating time compared to RALH, but experienced a higher incidence of transient hematuria.
mod_finding: A history of vaginal delivery was more prevalent in the tVRALH group and was identified as a factor influencing a surgeon's decision to choose tVRALH, while a history of cesarean delivery was less common in this group.
